findings.passage: Mr. Speaker, the SAVE Act is back before the House today, and right along with it is yet another attempt at voter suppression. It is no coincidence that this is happening right before the midterm elections.
findings.note: House floor remarks transcribed by Grabien (a media clip service, not the House record). Exact floor date not shown on the page; year inferred from the reference to the coming midterms and a January raid on the Fulton County election office. She links the SAVE Act to the midterms.

findings.passage: The SAVE Act would make it harder for millions of Americans to get registered to vote by requiring in-person registration at elections offices, government offices with government hours, y’all.
findings.note: House floor remarks transcribed by Grabien. The page gives no date; remarks refer to a January FBI action in Fulton County and to the SAVE America Act, which the House took up in February 2026. Speaks on SAVE Act registration rules.

findings.passage: DPOC policies would discard this foundational American right by forcing Americans to pay significant financial, administrative, and personal costs simply to participate in democratic elections, creating a modern day poll tax.
findings.note: Same press release (the page text sits in the page's embedded data); the sentence's speaker is not shown in the text I copied, so treat it as release text issued by her office.
subjects: documentary proof of citizenship to register

findings.passage: Undoubtedly, our election system needs strengthening. To that end we have introduced several reform bills like the John Lewis Voting Rights Act, the Expanding the Vote Act, the election Mail Act, and the People over Long Lines (POLL) Act. These measures would keep elections secure, accessible, efficient, and fair.
findings.note: Same letter and release. The letter names bills it says would strengthen elections, and says it opposes the documentary proof of citizenship petition.

findings.passage: The petition is part of a broader campaign, exemplified by Executive Order 14248 and the so-called SAVE Act, to manufacture disinformation about non-citizen voting as a pretext for shrinking the electorate.
findings.note: Same letter and release. She says claims about non-citizen voting are being used to justify rules that shrink the electorate.

findings.passage: Like any massive database, the information from the overhauled SAVE system will almost certainly include errors and other inaccurate information.
findings.note: Letter she led to the DHS Chief Privacy Officer about the SAVE database (a federal citizenship-status check, not the SAVE Act bill) being used to check voter rolls. Quoted from her official press release.

findings.passage: Some Texas counties are sending out SAVE non-citizenship notices  that require registered voters identified by SAVE as potential non-citizens to provide documentary proof of citizenship to remain registered—one county that examined its list of voters before sending out such notices found that about a quarter of the people listed had already provided proof of citizenship when they registered.
findings.note: Same letter. She cites Texas counties that asked flagged voters for proof of citizenship, and says it is a burden on the right to vote.

findings.passage: The use of the SAVE system for the purpose of determining voter eligibility is dangerous and unreliable, and it will be used as a tool against our democracy and free and fair access to the ballot.
findings.note: Official statement after a Supreme Court order allowing DHS to use the expanded SAVE database to check voter rolls. Date taken from the site feed entry for this post.

findings.passage: It made it harder to vote by mail, limited access to ballot dropboxes and early voting, let anyone challenge anyone else’s voter registration for any reason, and allowed the State Election Board to replace or override county election officials at will.
findings.note: Written testimony to the House Administration Committee Member Day (2023) about Georgia law SB 202. She says it made mail voting harder and allowed challenges to voter registrations. The testimony text does not mention photo ID.

findings.passage: The SAVE America Act is just another part of a scheme by House Republicans and the Trump Administration to take over our elections.
findings.note: Same floor remarks as above, as transcribed by Grabien (undated page).

findings.passage: Congresswoman Nikema Williams (GA-05) led a letter, along with 31 Congressional colleagues, to the General Council of the U.S. Election Assistance Commission to strongly oppose any changes to the national voter registration application that would add documentary proof of citizenship (DPOC) or “show your papers” requirements.
findings.note: Press release from her office about a letter to the Election Assistance Commission on adding documentary proof of citizenship to the federal registration form.
